subject: Benedict's Newsletter: No. 669
notes: Free edition, headed 'NO. 669 FREE EDITION SUNDAY 15 NOV 2026'; premium subscribers got it on Sunday 15 Nov, the free edition was sent on 17 Nov. Relative dates ('the 18th', 'Sunday evening') resolved to 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-15. The premium column is only a preview and is cut off mid-sentence.

stories.headline: Anthropic plans to raise $64bn at a $1.4tr valuation in its IPO, pricing on the 18th and trading the next day
stories.quote: Anthropic is planning to raise $64bn at a $1.4tr valuation in its IPO. It will price on the 18th and trade the next day.

facts.text: Planned IPO raise of $64bn at a $1.4tr valuation.
facts.quote: Anthropic is planning to raise $64bn at a $1.4tr valuation in its IPO.

facts.text: The IPO is due to price on the 18th and trade the next day (the 19th).
facts.quote: It will price on the 18th and trade the next day.

facts.text: Nvidia plans (or planned) to buy $10bn of stock in a $26bn private placement accompanying the IPO.
facts.quote: Also of note: Nvidia plans (planned?) to buy $10bn of stock in a $26bn private placement accompanying the IPO.

facts.text: In the marketing video Anthropic says it used Claude to get its models running on AMD's chip architecture in three days.
facts.quote: they used Claude to get their models running on AMD’s chip architecture in just three days, with ‘basically no human intervention’

facts.text: The author also discussed the financials of the Anthropic IPO on a podcast with Stephen Clapham.
facts.quote: I joined my friend financial analyst Stephen Clapham to discuss the financials of the Anthropic IPO.

stories.headline: Nvidia's board fired founder and CEO Jensen Huang; the CFO is temporary CEO
stories.quote: Unless you’ve been living in a hole, you’ll know that Nvidia’s board fired the founder and CEO, Jensen Huang, after discovering that not only had he been having an affair with the founder of a customer who may or may not be a Chinese intelligence asset

facts.text: The board also found he had affairs with at least two Nvidia employees and lied about that to the board.
facts.quote: but also had affairs with at least two Nvidia employees and lied about that to the board

facts.text: The CFO is temporary CEO while the board looks for a new leader.
facts.quote: Meanwhile, there’s a temporary CEO (the CFO, who Huang apparently belittled recently), while the board looks for a new leader.

facts.text: The customer in question is Megaspeed, which may have been shipping chips directly to China.
facts.quote: Megaspeed was one of these - but may also simply have been shipping the chips directly to China anyway.

facts.text: 20% of Nvidia revenue was going through Singapore before it stopped disclosing the number.
facts.quote: 20% of revenue was going through Singapore before it stopped disclosing the number - why?

facts.text: The FT reports Huang is talking to shareholders about getting his job back.
facts.quote: And... on Sunday evening, the FT reports that Huang is talking to shareholders about getting his job back.

stories.headline: Google announced smart glasses with camera, microphone, speaker and AI assistant, but no display
stories.quote: Google announced its own smart glasses: following Meta, these have a camera, microphone, speaker, and an AI assistant, but no display

facts.text: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports Apple is planning similar glasses that might arrive in 2027.
facts.quote: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports similar glasses in planning, that might arrive in 2027.

stories.headline: United joined the companies blocking consumer shopping agents
stories.quote: This week United added itself to the list of companies blocking this, explicitly for two reasons: first operational questions of security and liability, which are in principle solvable, but second because, in the CEO’s words, “we don’t want to create another middleman”

stories.headline: Reddit, moving to a logged-in only experience to stop LLM scraping, will launch its own reviews product
stories.quote: Reddit, which last week said it would transition to a logged-in only experience to stop LLMs scraping its content, will launch its own reviews product.

stories.headline: OpenAI launched a payment wallet and a way for businesses to claim their identity inside ChatGPT
stories.quote: Meanwhile, OpenAI launched a new payment wallet (trying to solve some of those liability questions), its ad business launched a way for businesses to claim their identity inside ChatGPT, Google expanded AI Overview ads, and the IAB launched a white paper on how ad attribution might work.

stories.headline: Anthropic launched a way for Claude to join video calls and generate documents, whiteboards and spreadsheets
stories.quote: Anthropic launched a way for Claude to join your video calls and dynamically generate documents, whiteboards and spreadsheets based on the ongoing conversation.

stories.headline: Microsoft's Office 365 went down for a day and a half
stories.quote: Half the enterprises on earth got a day off as Microsoft’s Office 365 went down for a day and half, prompting an extremely obvious joke.

stories.headline: The US air traffic control system shut down for a couple of hours after a copper-to-fibre upgrade went wrong
stories.quote: The US air traffic control system had to shut down for a couple of hours, apparently after an upgrade from copper comms to fibre went wrong.
